about: List prices in US dollars per million tokens, one entry per model id, read by scripts/lib/prices.py. Each entry carries its five component prices, the date they were confirmed in force at the source (effective) and where they were read (source). Anthropic first-party API rates: Amazon Bedrock and Vertex AI price separately, and US-only inference (inference_geo) multiplies every component by 1.1 on Claude 4.6 and later models; OpenAI's for the models behind Codex CLI, OpenCode's for its Console (Zen) models, xAI's for Grok and Cursor's for Composer, each from that provider's own page, where a component the provider does not bill separately carries the rate it bills it at. Grok and Composer are listed under the id each harness's reading carries: the --model slug a Cursor lane passes, since Cursor CLI prints no model (grok-4.7, grok-4.6 and grok-4.5, the Grok models Cursor's page offers, and composer-2.5), and OpenCode's <provider>/<model> id for each model on xAI's Text API table (xai/grok-4.7, xai/grok-build-0.1). premium_request is GitHub's price of one Copilot premium request, beside the token prices and never summed into them. A model not listed is reported as not priced, never as free. A project adds a model or replaces one under pricing.models in sdlc-studio/.config.yaml (reference-config.md#pricing).

models.source: https://cursor.com/docs/models-and-pricing (Cursor models table, Composer 2.5, standard speed, where https://cursor.com/docs/models redirects, read 2026-11-09)
models.note: the --model slug a Cursor lane passes and its reading carries (the Model ID on Cursor's Composer 2.5 page); the rates for usage beyond a paid plan's weekly pool. The page lists no cache-write price, so a token written to the cache is billed as input and both cache-write slots carry the input rate. Composer 2.5 (Fast), which the page makes the product default, bills $3 input, $0.50 cached input and $15 output, and a slug cannot tell it apart: a Fast session is under-priced here

premium_request.note: the legacy request-based price: since 1 June 2026 GitHub bills Copilot by tokens in AI credits, and premium requests remain the billing unit only of a Copilot Pro or Pro+ annual plan kept on request-based billing
